title: CASE Expression — Salary Bands
description: Categorize employees into salary bands using a CASE expression.

data.text: Write a query to assign each employee to a salary band: Junior (< 50k), Mid (50k–80k), Senior (80k–120k), or Executive (> 120k).

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
SELECT
    EmployeeID,
    FirstName,
    LastName,
    Salary,
    CASE
        WHEN Salary < 50000 THEN 'Junior'
        WHEN Salary < 80000 THEN 'Mid'
        WHEN Salary < 120000 THEN 'Senior'
        ELSE 'Executive'
    END AS SalaryBand
FROM Employees
ORDER BY Salary DESC;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: CASE evaluates conditions in order and returns the first matching result. Simple CASE uses a single expression; searched CASE (shown here) allows arbitrary conditions. Always include an ELSE to handle unmatched cases — NULL is returned if no WHEN matches and ELSE is absent.
